sources.entry: App Fair - Find and install macOS apps from Homebrew Cask and Fairground App catalogs.

summary.one_liner: App Fair is a macOS 12 app for browsing, searching, downloading, installing, and updating apps from appsource catalogs and Homebrew cask repositories.
summary.what_it_does: App Fair.app lets users browse, search, install, and update macOS applications from a selection of online app catalogs. It draws on appsource catalogs and Homebrew cask repositories as its sources. The README says the app can be downloaded from appfair.app or the GitHub releases page, and can also be installed via Homebrew with a single command. Translators can contribute localized strings through a Weblate interface. The README says updates to App Fair itself are downloaded and installed automatically when a new release is created and older clients next launch or refresh their catalogs. The app is signed and notarized, and it is not sandboxed because it needs to install other apps.
use_cases: browse an app catalog on a Mac
update installed Mac apps from one place
install Homebrew cask apps through a GUI
notable: Browses both appsource catalogs and Homebrew cask repositories in one app
Updates itself automatically when new releases are published
Signed and notarized, but intentionally not sandboxed so it can install other apps
Built and maintained with the appfair.net publishing system
caveats: Not sandboxed, which the README says is necessary for installing other apps
